The 3 crises we solve

Australia faces interconnected challenges.
OutbackNest addresses all three simultaneously.

Housing Crisis

1 in 8 Australians in housing stress

Median home prices have outpaced wages 6:1. An entire generation is locked out of ownership. Renters spend 30-50% of income on shelter.

122,494

Australians experiencing homelessness on any given night, with numbers rising each year.

Waste Emergency

1 million tonnes Plastic waste

of plastic sent to Australian landfill annually (Dept. of Environment)

200 million tonnes Mining tailings

of iron-rich tailings sit in waste dams across NSW, QLD, and WA, a stranded environmental liability, costing miners money to store.

Carbon Problem

15.3 tonnes CO₂ per capita in Australia

Among the highest in the developed world.

39% Of global CO₂ from buildings

The built environment is the single largest contributor to climate change. Cement alone accounts for 8% of global emissions — more than all aviation combined.

About OutbackNest

A social impact enterprise transforming environmental waste into durable, carbon-negative shelter for urban, regional, and remote communities across Australia.

Company overview

OutbackNest is a social impact enterprise operating under NestEffect Group in partnership with the ACNC-registered NestEffect Foundation (SERA Conteh Foundation).

Our business directly addresses Australia's housing crisis by utilizing advanced 3D-printing technology and repurposed waste materials to construct durable, fire-resistant, termite-proof, and carbon-negative homes at up to 40% less cost than traditional construction.

Built on a unique social impact model, 100% of profits from home sales fund free housing for vulnerable populations, turning environmental waste into permanent, sustainable shelter where it is needed most.

SERA Conteh Foundation ACNC Registered ASIC Registered
Our Model

Every home sold funds

A SERA Social Impact Enterprise

Vision and mission

Our Vision

A world where homelessness no longer exists.

Where every Australian — regardless of background, income, or circumstance — has access to safe, secure, and sustainable housing. Where women fleeing violence find sanctuary, regional communities thrive, and the planet is healed through the homes we build.

Our Mission

To end homelessness in Australia, and eventually the world.

By delivering rapidly deployable, affordable, carbon-negative homes to those who need them most. Using advanced 3D printing technology and waste materials, we build homes that are fire-resistant, termite-proof, and up to 40% cheaper than traditional construction. Every home sold funds another home gifted free to vulnerable women, children, and families.

The SERA Way

Our Values

At OutbackNest, everything we do is guided by The SERA Way — five core values that define who we are, how we build, and why we exist.

S

Sustainability

We build from waste — diverting plastic and mining tailings from landfill while removing carbon from the atmosphere. Every home is carbon-negative.

E

Equity

Housing is a right, not a privilege. We prioritise women fleeing violence, Indigenous communities, and families priced out of the market.

R

Resilience

Our homes survive bushfires, termites, and extreme heat. We build for the Australian climate — not against it.

A

Affordability

We deliver homes for $45,000–$150,000 — a fraction of the cost of traditional builds — and we are working to lower costs further.

A

Accountability

Profits fund the SERA Conteh Foundation's mission to gift homes free to those in crisis. Every dollar is accounted for in our annual impact reports.

The Collection

Seven models. One mission.

From the compact Nest Pod to the flagship Sovereign Nest, every model is 3D-printed, carbon-negative, and ready for regional delivery. Prices range from $45K to $150K.

Pricing is indicative only and subject to change based on design, site conditions, and project requirements.

Who We Build For

Women and children fleeing domestic violence. Homeless families on waiting lists. Indigenous communities without safe housing. Families priced out of every market.

Every commercial home sale directly enables a free home to be gifted through the SERA Conteh Foundation. When you buy with OutbackNest, you build twice.

Regional employment

By Year 3, OutbackNest will create 100 direct jobs in regional Australia, with projections reaching 220+ jobs by Year 5. These are skilled manufacturing, engineering, and construction roles that revitalize local economies.

Every home we build supports local communities through employment, training, and economic development.

Environmental impact

Each OutbackNest home removes an average of 3.3 tonnes of CO₂e from the atmosphere. We divert 2,500 tonnes of plastic waste and repurpose 500 tonnes of mining waste annually.

Our homes don't just reduce emissions — they actively heal the planet while providing safe shelter.
